## Summary

Operator-run end-to-end verification on a real Steam account that automatic follow detection unlocks the bonus game, plus a graceful-degradation re-check. Satisfies parent AC2.

**Status: awaiting operator execution (2026-09-30).** The agent cannot run this: it needs a **Windows x64 host with a real Steam client and account**, which is not provisioned in the agent environment. Per the producer, do **not** assume the client is logged in — verify both the logged-in automatic path and the not-logged-in / Steam-absent fallbacks. The implementation (P1–P5) is complete and pushed to `dev`; `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` is updated with the automatic-detection path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the addon built into the package and Steam **logged in**, `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end (designated bonus unlocked, no manual claim).
- [ ] With the addon present but **no user logged in**, the launcher does not crash, `isFollowing` returns `false`, the bonus stays locked, and the manual claim remains available (no fabricated follow).
- [ ] The unlock persists across a relaunch without re-verification.
- [ ] With Steam absent, the launcher boots, the bonus stays locked, and every non-gated game remains playable (no crash).
- [ ] Evidence (screenshots/notes) is recorded and the known-limitation note in `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` is removed or updated (already rewritten in P5; confirm on the real build).
- [ ] Parent `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1` AC2 is satisfied.

## Operator Steps

1. On Windows x64: `npm install steamworks.js && npm run build:steam-friends && npm run package:steam`.
2. Execute `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` (sections 1–6), recording Pass/Fail/N/A and evidence per step.

## Goal
Add a GitHub Actions job to `.github/workflows/package.yml` that automatically promotes the Windows installer to a draft GitHub Release when a `v*` tag is pushed to `main`.

## Context
- The `package.yml` workflow already builds and uploads the Windows installer on `push` to `main` and `v*` tags.
- The existing `.pi/skills/release-windows/scripts/promote-windows-release.mjs` helper script is a pure Node.js ESM module with zero dependencies — it is the perfect candidate for use in CI.
- The workflow triggers on `v*` tags specifically when the ship skill merges `dev` → `main` and tags the release.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Promotion job runs on tag push** — When a `v*` tag is pushed to `main`, the promotion job runs (it may skip for `main` branch pushes without tags).
- **Draft release created** — The job calls the existing promote script (not `--dry-run`) to create a draft release with the installer attached and CHANGELOG notes.
- **Non-blocking** — A promotion failure does NOT cancel or fail the workflow; use `continue-on-error: true` so the Pages deploy path is unaffected.
- **Idempotent** — If a draft release already exists for the version, the script reports the existing URL and exits 0.
- **Works in CI** — The script uses `gh` which is pre-installed on GitHub Actions runners; no extra setup needed.

## Key Files
- `.github/workflows/package.yml` — add the promotion job
- `.pi/skills/release-windows/scripts/promote-windows-release.mjs` — existing helper, invoked as-is

## Implementation
1. Add a new job `promote-release` after `package-windows` in `package.yml`.
2. The job depends on `package-windows:success` (runs only after a successful build).
3. The job uses `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` to run only on tag pushes.
4. Run the existing promote script (the script handles download + release creation internally).
5. Set `continue-on-error: true` so the workflow never fails due to promotion issues.
data.title: Add promotion job to package.yml CI workflow

# Debug Settings indicator + toggle for ToneForge

## Problem Statement

When running a game (e.g. the engine launcher with `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street`, or the standalone `../tce-main-street` app), there is **no way to tell whether ToneForge runtime synthesis is active** or whether audio is silently falling back to the Phaser/WAV path.

The Settings panel already has a dev-only **Debug Tools** section (`src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, gated by `isDevMode()` / `import.meta.env.DEV`), but none of its entries reports audio-synthesis state. This made it impossible to verify at runtime that the ToneForge wiring (`MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV`) is actually in use — the operator could only guess from the sound.

## Users

- **Engine developer**: *"As an engine developer, I want to see at a glance whether the ToneForge synth integration is active in the running game, so I can verify synthesis wiring without guessing from the sound."*
- **Game developer**: *"As a game developer, I want to toggle ToneForge on and off at runtime so I can A/B compare synthesised audio against the fallback audio."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In dev mode (`isDevMode()` / `import.meta.env.DEV`) the Settings panel Debug Tools section shows a **ToneForge** entry whose status text reports whether synth integration is currently active (`Active` / `Inactive`), together with diagnostic detail: whether the runtime module loaded, the factory count, and the last load error when it failed.
2. The status updates **live** while the panel is open (e.g. when the async module load finishes or when the user toggles it) — no need to close and reopen the panel.
3. Activating the entry **toggles ToneForge on/off at runtime**:
   - *off* detaches the synth player/mapping from the active `SoundManager`, so keys fall back to the existing WAV/Phaser path;
   - *on* re-attaches the loaded synth player and mapping.
   - Toggling requires **no scene restart**.
4. `SoundManager` exposes a small, typed API to support this (e.g. `isSynthActive()` / a status snapshot in addition to the existing `setSynthIntegration`). No behaviour change for existing callers when the new API is unused.
5. The indicator is registered by the **engine** so it appears for Main Street without a game-specific registration change (the engine injects it into the effective debug-tool list in dev mode, alongside the existing engine-generic tools). It must be tree-shaken from production builds.
6. Unit tests cover: status when active, status when inactive, toggle detach/attach behaviour, and that the entry is not registered in production.
7. `npm run build` and the full test suite pass.

## Implementation Notes

- Relevant files: `src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` (Debug Tools section, ~line 805), `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` (default debug tools, ~line 295), `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts`.
- `DebugToolsEntry` currently exposes only a static `description`. A live status needs an additive extension — e.g. `description: string | (() => string)` plus a refresh/poll mechanism in `SettingsPanel` — or a dedicated status getter that the panel reads on a timer.
- The tool needs a live reference to the scene's `SoundManager`. `soundManager` is `protected` on `CardGameScene`, but `initSettingsPanel` is a `CardGameScene` method, so a closure such as `() => this.soundManager` can be captured when the entry is built.
- Keep the design generic (any game with synth integration benefits); the Main Street loader is just the current consumer.

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV** (sibling) — Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module via a static-specifier import.
- **CG-0MOJ2OU7Y008QI36** — Enable true runtime on-the-fly synth playback for Main Street tf integration.
- **CG-0MUL2G17U003C1N6** — Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it).
- Companion work item: *ToneForge is not active at runtime* (filed alongside this one) — the indicator is the verification tool for that fix.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: `SettingsPanel` renders its content once; a live status requires either polling or an event. *Mitigation*: prefer a short poll only while the panel is open (and only in dev mode), or have the toggle refresh the text immediately and a single timer refresh for the async load.
- **Assumption**: dev-only availability is acceptable (matches the existing Debug Tools section). Production bundles stay unchanged.
data.title: Debug Settings: show whether ToneForge is active and allow toggling it

# ToneForge is not active at runtime — synth audio falls back to Phaser/WAV

## Problem Statement

Running Main Street (the engine launcher with `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street`, and the standalone `../tce-main-street` app) does **not** use ToneForge runtime synthesis. Despite the committed runtime synth module shipping and being importable, `SoundManager` never ends up with an active synth player, so synth-mapped effects play via the Phaser/WAV fallback (or not at all). The operator could only tell something was wrong from the sound, because nothing reports the state at runtime.

This is a regression of the intent of **CG-0MOJ2OU7Y008QI36** ("Enable true runtime on-the-fly synth playback") and **MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV** ("Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module via a static-specifier import").

## Evidence Gathered So Far

- `../tce-main-street/src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts` — `loadMainStreetTfModule()` wraps the dynamic import in an empty `catch` that sets `cachedLoadedModule = null`. **Any** load/normalisation failure is therefore silent, with no warning and no diagnostic state.
- `../tce-main-street/src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` (~line 207) initialises `SoundManager` with a `synthPlayer` that is `null` at runtime (`getMainStreetTfModule()` only reads the test-injection global `__MAIN_STREET_TF_MODULE__`), then attaches the real player asynchronously (~line 214):
  ```ts
  void loadMainStreetTfModule().then((loadedModule) => {
    if (!loadedModule || !s.soundManager) return;
    s.soundManager.setSynthIntegration(createTfPlayer(loadedModule), MAIN_STREET_TF_SFX_MAPPING);
  });
  ```
  If `loadedModule` is `null`, or `s.soundManager` is not the live instance at that moment, the attach is silently skipped.
- The committed module **is** served correctly (verified in dev): engine launcher resolves the specifier to `/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` and the standalone sibling to `/core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`; both return `200`, `text/javascript`, ~39 kB, with `tone` resolved. So the failure is **not** a missing/mis-served module file — it is in the wiring/normalisation/caching path.
- `SoundManager` exposes no runtime getter for synth state, so the failure cannot be observed without instrumentation (see companion indicator work item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The **root cause** is identified and documented on this work item: the exact step that prevents `SoundManager` from receiving an active synth player, with the evidence used (console output, network tab, or test reproduction).
2. ToneForge is **active at runtime**: after the game boots and the async load settles, `SoundManager` holds a non-null synth player and the Main Street synth key map, and a synth-mapped key (e.g. `sfx-deal` → `card-draw`) is routed through `tfAdapter` rather than the Phaser/WAV path.
3. Failures are **no longer silent**: if the module cannot be loaded or normalised, a clear warning is logged with the reason (and is surfaced by the debug indicator), replacing the bare `catch`.
4. The existing WAV/Phaser fallback still works when ToneForge is genuinely unavailable, and when it is toggled off via the debug indicator.
5. Automated tests assert that once `loadMainStreetTfModule()` resolves with the committed module, `SoundManager` receives a synth player and a synth-mapped `play()` delegates to it (and that a load failure leaves the fallback intact and logs a warning).
6. Manually verified in a browser (engine `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street` **and** standalone `../tce-main-street`) that synth audio is audible and the debug indicator reads **Active**.
7. `npm run build` and the full test suite pass; changes pushed to `dev` (sibling and/or engine as applicable) with commits recorded on the work item.

## Cross-repo Note

The loader and scene wiring live in the sibling repo `../tce-main-street`, while the synth integration contract (`SoundManager`, `tfAdapter`, runtime module) lives in this engine repo. This item is filed in the engine because the engine owns that contract, but it is expected to require a sibling change, which must be recorded here (commit hash + submodule bump if the engine is affected).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV** (sibling) — Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module via a static-specifier import (the change whose runtime effect is not materialising).
- **CG-0MOJ2OU7Y008QI36** — Enable true runtime on-the-fly synth playback for Main Street tf integration.
- **CG-0MUL2G17U003C1N6** — Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it).
- **CG-0MQR54BSD007FQTA** — graceful handling for a missing synth module (source of the silent-degradation behaviour).
- Companion work item: *Debug Settings indicator + toggle for ToneForge* (filed alongside this one) — the verification tool for this fix.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: The root cause may differ between the engine launcher and the standalone sibling app. *Mitigation*: reproduce in both and record which paths diverge; fix the shared contract rather than one caller.
- **Risk**: Silent-failure removal could surface a load error that was previously hidden; that is desired, and the fallback must remain so audio does not break.
- **Assumption**: The committed runtime module is the correct/authoritative source and does not need regenerating.
data.title: ToneForge is not active at runtime — synth audio falls back to Phaser/WAV
